# hunch auth: examples

`auth` signs in once per machine, so `check`, `find` and `eval` work in every directory with no `.env.local` and no linked Vercel project. None of these directories is a repository or has a config.

<!-- case: auth-status-none -->
### Nothing to sign in with

Exit 1 is the answer "no", not a crash.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth status
```

Exit code **1**.

stdout:

```text
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY   not set
TYPESAFE_API_KEY     not set
Vercel project       none
SemIf                not set up

Nothing to sign in with. Run `hunch auth login` to store a key, `hunch auth login --vercel`, or `hunch auth login --provider semif`, once for every directory.
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: auth-login-token -->
### Store a key without a terminal

The key arrives on standard input, as in `hunch auth login --with-token < key.txt`, never as an argument. At a terminal, plain `hunch auth login` asks with a hidden prompt instead.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth login --with-token
```

Exit code **0**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: stored AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in ~/.config/hunch/credentials (owner-only). It was not checked against the provider; the next check or find will be.
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: auth-login-no-terminal -->
### No terminal and no --with-token

An agent cannot answer a hidden prompt, and should not hold the key: ask the user to run `auth login` themselves.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth login
```

Exit code **2**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: no terminal to ask at. Pipe the key in: `npx @kelbie/hunch auth login --provider typesafe --with-token < file` (or --provider gateway).
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: auth-status-stored -->
### Signed in, from any directory

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth status
```

Exit code **0**.

stdout:

```text
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY   set, from ~/.config/hunch/credentials
TYPESAFE_API_KEY     not set
Vercel project       none
SemIf                not set up
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: auth-status-json -->
### The same, for a script

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth status --reporter json
```

Exit code **0**.

stdout:

```json
{
  "credentialsFile": "~/.config/hunch/credentials",
  "keys": {
    "AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY": "stored",
    "TYPESAFE_API_KEY": "missing"
  },
  "vercelLinked": false,
  "vercelProject": null,
  "semif": {
    "configured": false,
    "python": "python3",
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B",
    "revision": "851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a",
    "mode": "direct",
    "backend": "torch",
    "from": "nothing"
  },
  "credentialsFileReadableByOthers": false
}
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: auth-login-vercel-unlinked -->
### --vercel outside a linked directory

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth login --vercel
```

Exit code **2**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: no Vercel project is linked here. Run this inside a directory linked with `vercel link`, or pass --project and --team.
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: auth-logout -->
### Sign out

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch auth logout
```

Exit code **0**.

stderr:

